KEY MESSAGE 1...

Drizzle and light rain will gradually taper off into this evening as 
the weak cold front presses south and east. The latest satellite 
loop shows plenty of low clouds in place across NY and PA this 
afternoon, fading to higher, thinner clouds over southern Ontario. 
The main forecast challenge tonight will be just how much partial 
clearing the area sees and therefore how much fog may form. 
Northerly winds also look to remain steady between 3-8 mph much of 
the night, but could decouple in the deeper valleys. Depending on 
how thin the higher clouds get will also impact temperatures 
overnight. The latest forecast sticks with the NBM ensemble bland, 
which brings quite cool conditions, with lows in the upper 30s to 
40s for Central NY, and mid-40s to mid-50s for NE PA.

On Monday there will initially be some low level moisture trapped 
below 2500 feet agl over the  region in the morning, with broken to 
overcast stratus clouds expected. By early afternoon the low level 
moisture mixes out, but high level clouds develop between 20k to 35k 
feet agl. Overall, this should generally mean mostly cloudy 
conditions for most of the day, but some filtered sunshine is also 
expected to occur. Temperatures will be seasonable in the 60s for 
highs. Northerly winds are slightly breezy between 6-15 mph through 
the day.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

The latest 12z model guidance is starting to come into better 
agreement on the forecast details Monday night into Tuesday as a 
wave of low pressure moves slowly east across Pennsylvania. Clouds 
should increase Monday evening, with rain developing over NE PA 
during the mid to late evening hours. The steadiest rain will be in 
and around the Wyoming valley area, continuing into the overnight 
hours (where around a half inch is expected by morning). The rain 
looks to extend northward very close to the NY/PA border, with the 
exact northward extent still uncertain...but probably close to the 
Rte 17/I-86 corridor. Some periodic light rain continues into 
Tuesday morning, while gradually shifting south and west as high 
pressure advects in drier air from the northeast. Other than a few 
lingering showers or sprinkles over the Wyoming Valley the area 
should dry out by Tuesday afternoon; but clouds will linger in NE 
PA. Further north across the rest of Central NY confidence is 
increasing that it will remain dry for this time period, with mostly 
cloudy conditions Monday night becoming mostly sunny Tuesday 
afternoon. Temperatures will vary considerably, with cool overnight 
lows in the 40s Monday night in most locations. On Tuesday it looks 
to range from the mid-50s to low 60s in NE PA, with low to mid-60s 
for most of Central NY (outside of the higher elevations, which may 
stay in the 50s). Winds remain out of the northeast for this 
timeframe, generally between 5 to 15 mph.

There will be a sharp south to north gradient in rainfall amounts 
Monday night into Tuesday. Expect potentially between 1 to 1.5 
inches along and south of I-80 in NE PA, fading to a third of an 
inch near I-84 and less than a tenth of an inch for the NY/PA border 
region (Twin Tiers). This is still a tricky forecast when it comes 
down to pinning the exact rainfall amounts and locations...so please 
check back as we monitor and adjust for the latest model trends.

KEY MESSAGE 3...

There is now high confidence in the latest guidance that an 
expansive surface high and subtle rising 500mb heights will be over 
the area Wednesday into Thursday. This should provide dry, and partly 
to mostly sunny conditions both days for the entire forecast area. 
Low level winds remain out of the east-northeast so temperatures 
look to remain seasonable in the 60s for highs. Overnight lows could 
be chilly, in the upper 30s to mid-40s in most locations. Can't rule 
out some patchy frost for the normally colder locations if skies can 
clear and wind decouple enough.

KEY MESSAGE 4...

A complex weather pattern sets up late in the week into next 
weekend. A piece of upper level energy dives south out of Quebec 
into the local area. At the same time a closed upper level low 
drifts east across the Ohio Valley and off the Mid-Atlantic coast. 
By Friday morning these feature could phase/combine into a stronger 
mid and upper level low off the Delmarva region. Surface 
cyclogenesis occurs with a deepening low taking shape. There remains 
much uncertainty on where this low could ultimately develop and 
track. There is some potential for wrap around rain to push back to 
the west into some of our eastern forecast zones Friday into 
Saturday. Again, a lot of uncertainty and differences remain in the 
deterministic guidance. Ensembles means are beginning to pick up on 
this low development though, and this possible coastal low will 
certainly be tracked closely over the coming week.
